Pre-existing diseases carry a 36-month waiting period unless Aurora explicitly waives it in writing on the policy schedule [3]. This waiting period runs from the date of first policy commencement, provided coverage has been continuous without a break of more than 30 days [1].
The grace period for an annual policy is 30 days from the renewal due date [1].
As of 1 April 2026, the Aurora network covers 11,400 hospitals across 780 towns [1].

Under the Aurora Gold plan, the no-claim bonus is 25% of the base sum insured per claim-free year, accumulating to a maximum of 100% [1]. If a claim is made, the bonus is not reduced, but it stops accumulating for that year only [1].
No, you cannot claim for IVF treatment. Under the policy's treatment-related exclusions, infertility, assisted reproduction, and IVF are listed as permanent exclusions [1].
Under the Aurora Gold plan, the sub-limit for cataract surgery is ₹75,000 per eye [1].

If you are not satisfied with the Stage 1 outcome, you can escalate the matter to Aurora's Grievance Redressal Officer (GRO) [2]. If Aurora's final response is unsatisfactory or if Aurora has not responded within 30 days of your original complaint, you may approach the Insurance Ombudsman for your region [1].
Ambulance cover is ₹5,000 per hospitalisation, which applies to road ambulance only across all plans [1].

Yes, in-patient treatment for mental illness is covered on the same terms as physical illness, as required by the Mental Healthcare Act 2017 [1]. The standard 30-day initial waiting period applies, but there is no separate waiting period for it [1].

The free-look period is the window in which a new policy can be returned or cancelled for a refund [2, 3]. It lasts 15 days from receiving the policy document, or 30 days if the policy was sold through distance marketing [1, 2]. Upon cancellation during this period, the policyholder receives a refund of the premium minus the proportionate risk premium for the period of cover, medical examination costs, and stamp duty [2].
You earn 150 wellness points for completing an annual health check-up [1].

A day-care procedure is a procedure that requires less than 24 hours of hospitalisation due to technological advances, making it payable despite the general 24-hour admission requirement [3]. Out-patient treatment is not considered a day-care procedure [3].
For a cashless emergency admission, the hospital must notify Aurora within 24 hours of admission [1].
No, Aurora does not use a Third Party Administrator (TPA) [1]. Instead, Aurora administers its own claims directly [1].
To qualify as a hospital under the policy, a facility must have at least 10 in-patient beds in towns with a population below 10 lakh, or at least 15 in-patient beds elsewhere [1].

No, everything will not be paid [1]. Under the Silver plan with a ₹5,00,000 sum insured, the room-rent limit is 2% of the sum insured, which is ₹10,000 per day [1, 2]. Because you chose a room at ₹15,000 per day, a proportionate deduction will apply based on an eligibility ratio of 0.667 (10,000 ÷ 15,000) [1].

Dependent parents can be covered under the Silver (at an extra premium), Gold, and Platinum plans, while the Bronze plan does not allow them [1]. When you add a parent, the overall premium is determined by the age of the eldest covered member, which often increases the cost more than purchasing an individual senior-citizen policy for that parent [4].

Credit for the waiting periods you have already served will carry over, but only up to the sum insured of your previous policy, including any accrued no-claim bonus [1], [2]. Any increase or incremental amount above the previous sum insured will be subject to fresh waiting periods [1], [2].

To continue coverage beyond the first 90 days, you must inform Aurora within 90 days of birth to add your newborn to the policy as a dependent [1]. Adding the newborn within this 90-day window is guaranteed-issue with no medical underwriting, whereas requests made after this period will treat the child as a fresh applicant [1].

Under the Aurora Silver plan, a claim in any year reduces your accumulated no-claim bonus by 10 percentage points [1]. It does not reset your accumulated bonus to zero [1].
Under the Gold plan, the limit for a Caesarean section is ₹1,00,000 per delivery [1]. If the hospital bills ₹1,60,000, you would pay ₹60,000 out of pocket [1].

No, knee joint replacement is not covered immediately unless it is required following an accident, which can be claimed immediately [1], [2]. For knee joint replacements other than those following an accident, there is a 24-month waiting period [1].

Total discounts are capped at 30% of the base premium [1]. However, the wellness discount (up to 15% at renewal) is applied last, after the cap, and is the only discount that may exceed this limit [1, 3].

Cashless access is not available at an excluded provider and will be denied at pre-authorisation [2], [3], [4]. However, denial of cashless is not a rejection of the claim, and your option is to seek reimbursement with pre-approval required [3], [4]. Under reimbursement, a claim from an excluded provider is payable only if the admission was a genuine emergency and no alternative facility was reachable [1].

Under general claim timelines, Aurora closes the claim if a response to a query is not received within 45 days [2]. For Aurora Motor Insurance claims, the deadline to respond to a query is 30 days from the date of the query [4].
A planned cashless admission must be notified at least 72 hours before admission [2], [3]. The pre-authorisation request is submitted by the hospital to Aurora [2], [3].

Aurora settles or rejects a complete reimbursement claim within 15 working days of receiving the last required document [1], [2]. If Aurora raises a query regarding the claim, the clock restarts when the requested document is supplied [1].

The **Aurora Gold** plan has no co-payment at all ages [1]. Additionally, the **Aurora Silver** plan has no co-payment when the eldest insured member is below age 60 (a 10% co-payment applies when the eldest member is above 60 years) [2].

Across the four plans, pre-hospitalisation cover is provided for 30 days, 45 days, 60 days, and 90 days, respectively [1]. Correspondingly, post-hospitalisation cover spans 60 days, 90 days, 120 days, and 180 days across the four plans [1].

You should choose the **Gold** plan, as it covers dependent parents-in-law [1] and removes room-rent sub-limits [3]. While the **Platinum** plan also covers dependent parents-in-law [1], the provided sources do not specify its room-rent terms.

Under Aurora indemnity plans, dental treatment and oral surgery are excluded unless necessitated by an accidental injury requiring hospitalisation [2], [3]. Additionally, out-patient dental work is specifically noted as not being covered by any plan [1].
